To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the perisynchaptic ECM affects the surface dynamics of AMPARs differently on spiny neurons and on aspiny neurons and that the lateral mobility of the AMPARs on the aspiny neurons is controlled by intracellular Ca2+.
the perisynthesis ECM does not affect AMPAR mobility on aspiny inter-neurons.
the perisynthesis extracellular matrix (e.g. hyaluronan) contributes to the immobilization of AMPA-type receptors at synapses on principal hippocampal spiny neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the lateral mobility of receptors on the neuronal membrane.
the lateral mobility of glutamate receptors in the postsynaptic membrane and its regulation by Ca2+ and the perisynaptically localized extracellular matrix.
the role of the perisynapse in the regulation of AMPAR dynamics at synapses on aspiny neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ECM is not involved in the regulation of AMPAR mobility on the short timescale in aspiny interneuronal shaft synapses.
the perisynthesis of the ECM is a major determinant for the lateral mobility of synaptic AMPARs at spines of principal neurons but is not relevant for shaft synapses of interneurons.
AMPAR mobility at the surface of aspiny neurons is not controlled by the ECM and instead is controlled by the intracellular Ca2+ concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AMPARs are mobile on aspiny neurons and their mobility is regulated by intracellular Ca2+.
the perisynthesis of GluA receptors is not affected by the perisynapic ECM, but rather the internal Ca2+ concentration.
the perisynthesis ECM contributes to the lateral mobility of synaptic receptors on spiny neurons and that the Ca2+-permissive environment in aspiny neurons determines receptor mobility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lateral mobility of synaptic AMPARs on spiny neurons is controlled by the perisynapic ECM, whereas Ca2+ controls receptor mobility on aspyn neurons.
the perisynthesis ECM is not required for the control of lateral receptor mobility.
the lateral mobility of synaptic AMPARs in aspiny interneuron shafts depends on the intracellular Ca2+ concentration and not the perisynaptically located ECM.
